findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic (replay race)
findings.body: In the credentials `authorize` handler, the backup code is checked against a value read earlier and then the whole re-encrypted array is written back with a plain update. There is no compare-and-set or transaction. Two concurrent logins using the same backup code both pass the check and both succeed, so a single-use code can be used more than once. A concurrent use of two different codes also loses one of the deletions, leaving a used code valid.

findings.title: Backup code compared with non-constant-time indexOf and no normalization
findings.body: `indexOf` performs a plain string comparison against the stored codes. The input is also not lowercased or trimmed, so a code typed in uppercase (the placeholder shows `XXXXX-XXXXX`) is rejected even though it is valid. A timing-safe comparison would also be preferable.

findings.title: Rate-limit error not mapped to a message
findings.body: Backup codes are 40-bit secrets, and their brute-force protection depends on the rate limit enforced in `authorize`. The login page has no specific mapping for the RateLimitExceeded error, so a rate-limited user only sees the generic "something went wrong" fallback instead of being told they have been rate limited.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode crashes handler
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called without checking the type. Any truthy non-string value (for example a number) throws a TypeError, which results in a 500 response instead of a 400.

findings.title: Plaintext backup codes remain in component state after close
findings.body: `resetState` clears the password, error and step, but not `backupCodes`, the secret, the QR data URI, or the blob URL. The codes and secret stay in memory, and the object URL is never revoked when the modal closes.

findings.title: formatBackupCode used before its declaration
findings.body: `handleSetup` calls `formatBackupCode`, which is a `const` arrow function declared later in the component body. This works only because `handleSetup` runs after render, so the code is fragile. Separately, `useState([])` infers the type `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and the mapping over codes are poorly typed.
